Sample.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/13] The participants were young people accessing services rather than those recruited by advertisement, and exclusion criteria were kept to a minimum to maximise generalisability.
Sample.warning: N for sample not reported in this section.

IPT.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/13] This study was carried out according to CONSORT guidelines, in a range of primary healthcare sites. It was adequately powered to address the primary question of whether SPARX was inferior to treatment as usual; the study may, however, have been underpowered to detect superiority over treatment as usual. ... An earlier pilot study (by a member of our group) of a computerised intervention, The Journey,15 which informed the development of SPARX, showed that it was more effective than a placebo computerised intervention (Cohen's d=1.7), and a companion study to this randomised controlled trial16 showed that SPARX was more effective than a waitlist situation in a group of young people excluded from mainstream education (Cohen's d=1.61).
IPT.warning: SPARX is described as a 'computerised intervention', which typically aligns with CBT principles. No mention of IPT.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/13] Ideally we would have liked to have used more than one measure on interview, and originally we planned to include an interview assessment of diagnosis, which would also have allowed us to assess for comorbidity. This proved to be difficult logistically because of the extra time needed and the difficulties fitting this in with the services participating in the trial.

Source.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/13] The primary outcome variable was assessed by research assistants blind to allocation. ... We made the children's depression rating scale-revised our primary outcome variable in line with most studies of antidepressant drugs in this age group.
